newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq to reduce workforce by 1,050.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq to reduce workforce by 1,050.

text.p: Bezeq Israel Telecom's board of directors has approved a plan presented by management that calls for the reduction of the company's work force by 1,050 employees within five years starting in 1997, a spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
By the end of this year Bezeq's work force will total just under 9,000 following the early retirement of 200 workers.
"The move to reduce our workforce is aimed at increasing our efficiency in order to compete in an environment of growing competition," Bezeq president Yitzhak Kaul said.
Bezeq currently competes only in the cellular field. However, Israel's international services are due to be opened to competition by the end of the year or in early 1997.
The Communications Ministry is expected to announce the winners in the tender for two additional providers of international phone services in the next few weeks.
The plan also calls for the state-controlled company to raise funds through an international share offering in 1997.

Communications Minister Limor Livnat held talks in New York last week with Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley. Merrill Lynch is acting as lead underwriter for the offering while Morgan Stanley is the adviser.
Israeli newspapers quoted Livnat as saying that an offering could take place as early as next spring.
